title: Steve Kerr's 13th Season Looms as Warriors Coach Appears Set to Run It Back - NewsBreak
text:
By Reign Amurao ,
31 minutes ago There are questions about Steve Kerr’s future with the Golden State Warriors . He is in the final year of his two-year, $35 million contract extension that he signed in 2024. The Warriors have not given him a new deal , and many are wondering what will happen to the head coach. Especially after the team missed the postseason for the fourth time in his 12-year tenure .
According to various reports, Kerr’s future with the Warriors is a conversation to be had over the summer. The longtime head coach is still interested in working as the team’s head coach. However, he knows that the decision will be on the organization’s front office.
Monte Poole of NBC Sports Bay Area reported on Wednesday that Steve Kerr had a positive discussion with the front office during their meetings last week. In those meetings, Kerr is said to still be interested in coaching Golden State in the future.
“Those meetings, per several league sources, included discussions not only about last season’s Warriors but also about the team’s future,” Poole wrote . “Kerr came across to some as if he was preparing to re-sign and be on the bench next season.”
The Warriors’ dynasty with Kerr, Stephen Curry and Draymond Green is likely past its prime. However, the team’s core wants to remain together and continue the twilight years of their careers in one organization.
A decision on Kerr’s future could likely be announced next week.
Steve Kerr Addresses His Verbal Spat With Draymond Green The past season has been filled with ups and downs for Steve Kerr and the Warriors. One of the incidents that became a hot topic for the team was the verbal spat between Kerr and star forward Draymond Green. It happened in December, during a game against the Orlando Magic, where Green crashed out and headed to the locker room.
“So then, for a long time, we had a truce. I understood him so well. He understood me,” Kerr said via The New Yorker. “But this year we had a major blowout in December. He’s such a unique person. There [are] things he’s done that I can never forgive him for, and yet I will do anything for him.”
Fortunately for the Warriors, the head coach and the star player have moved on from it.
